notes: §1985:XIV.3.6.3 SR6 (Amendment 1): "If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it must reference an alphanumeric function." BindSend binds a functionCall sendText through IntrinsicOperand and refuses (COBOL6171) any operand whose IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf is not alphanumeric: probes at --std 85 refuse ORD, ORD-MAX, LENGTH (integer), SQRT and RANDOM (numeric), and NATIONAL-OF (also COBOL1502, a 2002 function), and accept UPPER-CASE, LOWER-CASE of a subscripted element, REVERSE of a group, CHAR, CURRENT-DATE, WHEN-COMPILED and a reference-modified UPPER-CASE, in Format 1 and Format 2; the witness refuses FUNCTION ORD at line 32. LEAD outside this rule (no note found): the same check refuses a NON-function identifier-1 that is numeric (PIC 9(4)) or numeric-edited (ZZ9) at --std 85 with a 2002 rule (A.2.6.2 SR2), though the 1985 SEND has no class rule for a data item (rejects-legal-source against 1985-FMT-XIV.3.6.2).

next.reason: 1985 (rule added by Amendment 1, X3.23a-1989, Errata C159): 'If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it must reference an alphanumeric function' (§1985:XIV.3.6.3 SR6), on the FROM operand of the Communication module's SEND cd-name-1 ('Cd-name-1 must reference an output CD or input-output CD', §1985:XIV.3.6.3 SR1). 2023 has no communication facility and no cd-name: its SEND 'sends a message to a message server run unit' (§2023:14.9.38.1), a different statement, whose one rule on identifier-1 lists clauses its description 'shall not contain' (§2023:14.9.38.3 SR3). No 2023 rule restricts a function-identifier in a SEND, so the requirement is dropped with the feature, as the statement's other syntax rules were.
